Given the tenant's anxiety and stated email preference, I should respond through both the portal and email to make sure the message reaches them reliably. The bin issue is a council responsibility under Tower Hamlets, so that's outside what I can directly resolve.

For the engineer visit on 14 October, I'll note it as already on the job rather than creating a new ticket, confirming it's scheduled without asking unnecessary questions. I'll also check in on whether heating or hot water has actually gone out, framing it as a safety check and asking them to flag it immediately if it does fail.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, sorry for the wait on your boiler (R-4799). Where it stands: the first engineer visited and quoted £780 to replace a part called an expansion vessel, which is likely why the pressure keeps dropping. Your landlord asked for a second quote before agreeing to that spend, and a second company (Swift P&H) is noted to visit on 14 October. We're confirming that date with them and will tell you as soon as it's confirmed. Until then, no repair has been approved. If the boiler is still working, you can carry on topping up the pressure as before. If you lose heating or hot water, or see leaks or smells, tell us straight away. We'll update you again by Wednesday 14 October. On bins: collections are run by Tower Hamlets council, not us, so please check or report a missed collection on their website. I can't see your collection day from here. Anything else, just reply here.

I've also emailed you the details.
